title: When CURLOPT_INTERFACE (or the command line tool's --interface option) is set with one of the documented prefixes (if!, host!, ifhost!), that… (CVE-2026-107929)
description: A vulnerability exists in the handling of CURLOPT_INTERFACE (or the command line tool's --interface option) when set with certain prefixes (if!, host!, ifhost!). The binding to the source interface is not included in the connection reuse key, allowing a later transfer requesting a different source to reuse an existing connection and send traffic from the earlier transfer's source address.
aiSummary: CVE-2026-107929 describes a flaw in the connection reuse logic of software using CURLOPT_INTERFACE or the equivalent command line option. When the interface is specified with documented prefixes such as if!, host!, or ifhost!, the binding is omitted from the connection reuse key. This omission causes subsequent transfers that specify a different source interface to silently reuse an existing connection established with a different source address, potentially causing traffic to originate from an unintended source interface.
aiImpact: The vulnerability can cause network traffic to be sent from an unintended source interface due to connection reuse ignoring the interface binding. This may lead to unexpected network behavior or policy violations if different source interfaces are expected to segregate traffic. No direct exploitation or active attacks are reported in the wild.
